prompt: Some people believe that university students should be required to study subjects that are related to their main field of study, while others believe that they should be free to choose any subjects they are interested in. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is increasingly argued that university students should focus exclusively on subjects related to their main field of study. While there are reasonable arguments on both sides of this issue, I largely disagree with this view because studying broader subjects can develop valuable skills and prepare students for an unpredictable job market.

The strongest argument against restricting students’ choices is that exposure to different disciplines can broaden their intellectual abilities. This is largely because subjects outside a student’s major often require different ways of thinking, meaning that learners can develop skills such as critical thinking, creativity and effective communication. For instance, an engineering student who takes psychology or public speaking may become better at understanding people and presenting complex ideas clearly. Taken together, these factors demonstrate that a broader education can produce more versatile graduates, thereby strengthening the case for allowing students greater academic freedom.

A further consideration is that modern employment increasingly requires people to work across different fields. The underlying reason is that many professional roles involve a combination of technical knowledge and transferable skills, particularly when employees are expected to adapt to rapidly changing technologies and business practices. A case in point is a financial analyst who may need not only a strong understanding of economics but also knowledge of data analysis and computer science to perform effectively. Overall, this suggests that studying a wider range of subjects can improve graduates’ adaptability, which further supports the view that students should not be limited to courses directly related to their major.

In conclusion, although specialising in one’s main field may provide certain academic benefits, I remain convinced that university students should have the freedom to explore other subjects. This is primarily because broader study develops transferable abilities, while greater academic flexibility can help graduates adapt to changing professional demands.
